API and measurement lifecycle

Source: LIFECYCLE.md

Current distributions

The current development release is 0.5.0.9001. It includes all current guide workflows. Stable 0.4.0 remains available as a separate fixed release. Pin the package archive used in an analysis and use citation("ldfreq") to cite that exact version. New releases do not replace earlier fixed archives.

The release-scope guide explains supported inputs, optional integrations and compatibility. The NEWS records changes by version.

Reference data in 0.5.0.9001

Third-party reference data are optional downloads with their own licenses. Use lexdiv_resource_info() to inspect the terms, source, version and hash, then explicitly use lexdiv_download_resources(..., accept_license = TRUE). Ordinary computation and installation never download resources. The MIT code can be installed and used without obtaining MorphoLex or any other reference snapshot. Existing resource-based analyses need this one-time setup; the reference data bytes and measurement definitions are unchanged.

Rendered guides are published on the website. The compact package archive contains guide sources and installed example scripts; it does not include rendered outputs from the separately licensed reference data.

Metric identities and saved results

Package version, metric method ID, metric-contract version, result schema, preprocessing and reference-resource identity are separate. Preserve them with the original inputs and complete results. Changes in a package version do not relabel the methods or values inside an earlier saved result.

The current catalog has thirteen metrics: eleven defaults, opt-in mtld_ma, and experimental expected_ttr_d. MTLD-MA adds a separate method definition; it does not change ordinary MTLD or existing presets. Core contract 0.2.0 continues to describe the unchanged existing definitions and result schema. Adding an opt-in method does not invalidate plans for unchanged definitions.

For historical analyses, package 0.3.0 changed ordinary MTLD from a minimum-ten factor rule to no minimum and advanced the core contract from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0. The old rule remains an explicit variant. Do not mix old and new MTLD values under one method label. Plans from the old contract must be recreated; reading old RDS results does not require rewriting their identities or values.

Expected-TTR D remains an experimental curve estimator, not CLAN VOCD. Formula agreement, length sensitivity, sampling reliability and proficiency validity are distinct claims. The selection guide provides evidence and conditions for choosing among the implemented measures.

Naming and compatibility

General analysis functions use lexdiv_; resource-specific operations retain resource prefixes. Operation names put the action before its object. _text identifies raw text and _batch identifies separately named documents.

Current name Earlier compatible name
lexdiv_compare_ngrams() lexdiv_ngram_compare()
lexdiv_build_ngram_reference() lexdiv_ngram_reference_build()
lexdiv_screen_lengths() lexdiv_screen()
lexdiv_sort_concordance() lexdiv_concordance_sort()

These four pairs are exact aliases, with the same arguments and results. Study-table, concordance, collocation and keyness functions are public APIs; their earlier installed source helpers remain compatibility wrappers. Saved old records remain accepted by the corresponding operations. No implicit migration overwrites a saved record.

Ordination, readability, L2SCA import and teaching workflows remain explicitly sourced recipes. Their guides define the required inputs and external tools. Pin the package archive when using these scripts. Their availability does not imply automatic linguistic annotation or educational interpretation.

Change policy

A change to a formula, threshold rule, token selection or missingness meaning requires an identifiable method or contract change and migration documentation. An added optional operation should preserve existing defaults and result shapes. Document public renamings with compatibility aliases before removing old names. Errors in input types must be reported rather than silently coerced to scores; intended categorical metadata and legitimate missing results retain their roles.
